landmark_cases.title: Kousisis v. United States
landmark_cases.reason: Supreme Court endorsement of the fraudulent‑inducement theory under the federal fraud statutes; clarifies that obtaining money or property is the object of the scheme and that a net pecuniary loss to the victim is not required.

landmark_cases.title: Ciminelli v. United States
landmark_cases.reason: Rejects the right‑to‑control theory and reaffirms that federal fraud statutes protect traditional property interests, framing the property requirement central to this case.

landmark_cases.title: United States v. Greenlaw
landmark_cases.reason: Fifth Circuit articulation that §1348 securities fraud borrows from mail/wire fraud; sets out the scheme‑to‑defraud and intent‑to‑defraud elements for §1348.

landmark_cases.title: United States v. Evans
landmark_cases.reason: Defines in the Fifth Circuit what constitutes a scheme to defraud and the requisite intent to defraud (intent to deceive and to cause harm), principles applied to §1348.

landmark_cases.title: United States v. Baker
landmark_cases.reason: Clarifies that fraud liability does not require a mirror‑image loss/gain and that deprivation of money or property by materially false pretenses suffices.
